analysis.title: 5 risks for the global economy in 2027
key_insights: ING lists five risks to its 2027 outlook: an AI-triggered US equity bear market, second-round inflation effects from the energy shock, weather and critical infrastructure shocks, geopolitical de-escalation producing an energy peace dividend, and a worse bond market rout.

AI meltdown scenario: US tech correction becomes a deep bear market if AI demand disappoints (weak enterprise adoption), cheaper models arrive while corporates are wary of pricey tokens, and overcapacity plus higher financing costs trigger credit events outside the major hyperscalers.

Around a third of US growth has come from AI so far in 2026. As a rule of thumb, a further 30% equity drawdown would wipe out $24.5tr of household wealth, concentrated among high-income consumers who are less likely to cut spending, but who are also the only ones spending this time.
In the AI meltdown scenario, investment takes the bigger hit. Wider credit spreads would hit non-AI business investment, and non-tech investment fell more than tech investment after the dotcom bust.

ING says the AI-bust scenario is not 2008 because household and business balance sheets are healthier. The Fed would likely deliver sharp rate cuts. Chair Warsh is not convinced policy is currently restrictive, partly because equity markets are supported. If equities fall, a key pillar of the Fed's tightening cycle falls away. Impact: potential US recession, Europe less affected, curtailed Fed hiking cycle and faster cuts.
Baseline call is that second-round effects from the energy shock stay contained, letting major central banks cut rates toward the end of 2027. ING sees four ways this could be wrong.

Second-round risk 1: the lack of effects so far may reflect longer lags. Hedging and supply chain resilience built since 2022 erodes as the crisis lasts. Natural gas prices have spiked, so it is no longer solely an oil crisis. Food inflation could turn sharply through the winter, and new-year services price resets are the big test.

Second-round risk 2: the jobs market tightens, with vacancies rising while labour supply is constrained by low migration. Workers gain bargaining power and get bigger pay settlements or bonuses, which amplifies services inflation.

Second-round risk 3: prolonged Middle East escalation could take oil to $130/bbl or above this winter. Central banks have said energy prices and second-round effect probability are positively correlated.

Second-round risk 4: governments absorb the energy shock on their balance sheets with support to households and businesses despite rising borrowing costs. This eases the growth hit and may temper headline inflation, but adds to medium-term inflationary pressure.
Impact of the second-round scenario: core inflation stays well above target in 2027, rate hikes are more significant (proving market expectations right), and rate cuts are delayed.

Supply shocks are becoming more common this decade, supporting ING's view that inflation cycles are getting shorter. A severe El Niño could raise agricultural prices, though ING's research says this is not inevitable. Low Panama Canal water is a wildcard for shipping. On top of the energy shock, headline inflation could stay at 4%, especially in Europe, into 2028.

Critical infrastructure failure scenario: a cyberattack or cascading technical failure disabling power, payments, communications or cloud services across several European economies for days. Damage rises non-linearly with duration, frequency and reach. The 18-hour Spain outage in 2025 had little discernible GDP impact, but repeated outages would hit confidence and force firms to spend on resilience. Impact: lower growth, potentially higher inflation, more hawkish central banks.

De-escalation scenario: with Republicans weakened after the midterms and President Trump focused on his legacy, a US-driven settlement ends the Ukraine war early and enables broader accommodation with Russia, including phased sanctions relief. Better US-Russia relations allow faster Middle East diplomacy, including Russian support for an Iran settlement and tighter nuclear constraints.

Impact of de-escalation: a significant, durable fall in oil (especially diesel) and European gas prices. Inflation stays high in Q1 but falls below 2% by summer in the US and Europe, and central bank rate cuts are accelerated.

Bond rout scenario: ING's Rates Strategy team says US 10-year yields could reach 6% if US growth accelerates to 3-4%, the fiscal deficit worsens, or inflation fails to fall. Higher yields would stress the global financial system, worsen concerns about leveraged AI players and brake the US economy beyond the data centre rollout.

In the bond rout scenario, European public finances come under scrutiny amid a raft of elections and rising populism. French spreads blow out beyond 200bp and spill into Italian BTPs. Signs of contagion beyond France would push the ECB toward a more dovish tone, or an end to QT, but the bar for the Transmission Protection Instrument is not met. Impact: weaker US and European growth, central banks struggle to turn dovish if yields rise on inflation.
Context: US stocks fell sharply on 5 November 2026 on an AI and chip selloff that pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory.

sector_views.rationale: ING flags a downside risk scenario in which AI demand disappoints, overcapacity builds and credit events occur outside the hyperscalers. It is a risk scenario, not the base case.

Weather shocks (severe El Niño, low Panama Canal water) and critical infrastructure failures such as cyberattacks.

tension_points.theme: AI bust vs balance sheet resilience
tension_points.bull_case: Household and business balance sheets are healthier than in 2008, and the Fed would likely deliver sharp rate cuts, which cushions the damage.
tension_points.bear_case: A third of US growth has come from AI, high-income consumers are the only ones spending, and wider credit spreads would hit non-AI investment, which could mean a US recession.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Demand for AI disappoints, with weak enterprise adoption and cheaper models, leading to a further 30% equity drawdown and credit events outside the hyperscalers.

tension_points.bull_case: Second-round effects from the energy shock remain contained, so major central banks can cut rates toward the end of 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Lagged pass-through, a tightening jobs market, oil at $130/bbl or above and fiscal support push core inflation well above target in 2027 and delay cuts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Services price resets in the new year and food inflation through the winter would show second-round effects emerging.

tension_points.bull_case: The bar for the ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument is not met, and the ECB could ease through a more dovish tone or an end to QT if contagion spreads.
tension_points.bear_case: US 10-year yields at 6% and French spreads beyond 200bp would stress the financial system and hit growth in the US and Europe.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Signs of contagion beyond France would be a catalyst for ECB action.
